body.statement: Let \(G_0\) and \(G_1\) be finite directed acyclic graphs on the same labelled vertex set.  They have the same skeleton and the same unshielded colliders if and only if they are Markov equivalent.  If they are equivalent and \(m\) adjacencies have opposite orientations, then there is a sequence of exactly \(m\) distinct covered-edge reversals from \(G_0\) to \(G_1\); every intermediate graph is acyclic and equivalent, and each reversal corrects one original orientation disagreement.

source.verbatim_statement: Theorem 1 [Verma and Pearl, 1990] Two dags are equivalent if and only if they have the same skeletons and the same v-structures. Theorem 2 Let G and G' be any pair of dags such that G is equivalent to G'. There exists a sequence of |Delta(G,G')| distinct edge reversals in G with the following properties: (1) Each edge reversed in G is a covered edge. (2) After each reversal, G is a dag and G is equivalent to G'. (3) After all reversals, G = G'.

upstream.citation: Verma and Pearl (1990), Equivalence and Synthesis of Causal Models
upstream.locator: Theorem 1, as explicitly reproduced and attributed on Chickering 1995 page 90
